edges.description: Reproduces periventricular heterotopia and impaired neuronal migration via the Big2-FlnA axis.
edges.limitations: Recapitulates the migration/heterotopia arm but not the microcephaly that is a defining human feature, so it models only part of the disorder.

edges.description: Complete constitutive disruption of BIG2 is lethal in utero, so the mouse dies before cortical neuronal migration and cannot reproduce the migration-failure / heterotopia phenotype.
edges.limitations: Embryonic lethality precludes modelling the postnatal cortical malformation; the human disease results from LoF variants compatible with survival.

evidence.snippet: Here we show that an autosomal recessive condition characterized by microcephaly and periventricular heterotopia maps to chromosome 20 and is caused by mutations in the gene ADP-ribosylation factor guanine nucleotide-exchange factor-2 (ARFGEF2)

evidence.reference_title: ARFGEF2-Related Periventricular Nodular Heterotopia: A Case Report and Literature Review.

nodes.description: Homozygous nonsense variant reported in an affected child, consistent with the loss-of-function mechanism; this case also carried left ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy, widening the phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: The expanding phenotypic spectrum of ARFGEF2 gene mutation: Cardiomyopathy and movement disorder.

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in ARFGEF2 abolish or reduce the guanine nucleotide-exchange activity of BIG2 toward ARF GTPases, the first step that normally licenses vesicle budding from the trans-Golgi.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in ARFGEF2 implicate vesicle trafficking in neural progenitor proliferation and migration in the human cerebral cortex.
evidence.snippet: ARFGEF2 encodes the large (>200 kDa) brefeldin A (BFA)-inhibited GEF2 protein (BIG2), which is required for vesicle and membrane trafficking from the trans-Golgi network (TGN)

nodes.description: A gene-trap line with functional disruption of Arfgef2 is embryonic lethal, so constitutive total loss of BIG2 in the mouse cannot model the postnatal neurodevelopmental disease.

evidence.reference_title: Early embryonic lethality in gene trap mice with disruption of the Arfgef2 gene.
evidence.snippet: Our results indicate that murine BIG2 is essential for early embryonic development.

nodes.description: Arfgef2-null mice develop periventricular heterotopia with impaired neuronal migration, acting through increased FlnA phosphorylation; they recapitulate the migration/heterotopia arm but microcephaly is not reported.

evidence.reference_title: Brefeldin A-inhibited guanine exchange factor 2 regulates filamin A phosphorylation and neuronal migration.

nodes.description: The heterotopic grey matter and disrupted cortical architecture form an abnormal network that is prone to epileptogenesis and underlies the developmental, cognitive and motor impairment.

nodes.description: Impaired trans-Golgi trafficking blocks delivery of adhesion molecules such as E-cadherin and beta-catenin to the cell surface, disrupting the cell-cell and cell-scaffold adhesion that neurons and the neuroependymal lining need for migration.
